transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-30 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Collins (Argento CTO), Diego Ruiz (Argento Lead ML Eng), Priya Nair (Argento Infra)
Links referenced: Console demo recording (https://redwood.app/rec/abc123), Cost sheet (link sent in chat), SOC2/KMS brief (redwood.com/security/kms.pdf)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, welcome, thanks for taking the time. quick agenda — walk through the Optimize recommendations for batching and prefetch/prefix KV cache, then map that to argento's traffic and cost targets, questions along the way.

[01:05] Maya: thanks, Samir. yes, we've been curious about how prefetch helps with our product recommendations route. we run a short context, usually 120 tokens plus user history of maybe 800 tokens. latency budget is tight — 120 to 200 ms p90 ideally.

[02:30] Lena: got it. so two main levers we'll focus on — continuous batching and prefix/KV session prefetch. i'll show the console suggestions and then run a small econ sim with your rough TPS numbers.

[04:10] Diego: quick interruption — our peak is about 25 TPS for the rec route, but it's very spiky, 2x during promos. concurrency is currently bounded by our frontend to about 40 outstanding requests.

[05:00] Samir: perfect, that's in scope. first, a quick primer — prefetch or prefix cache keeps reused KV cache for the model across session turns. instead of re-computing the long context every request we load the KV and then only generate on shorter suffixes, which cuts effective token compute. the console Optimize tab will show recommended prefetch length and expected token savings.

[06:45] Priya: small note on security — we need to ensure prefetch doesn't persist PII in cache beyond retention policy; does the private deployment support vault-backed KMS?

[07:20] Lena: yes, on Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and set KV retention TTLs. For hosted we have encryption at rest and customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers; i'll attach the SOC2/KMS doc.

[08:50] Maya: what's the typical cost delta — like numbers. we've been charged roughly $0.0004/token on our current vendor for large models; curious what the per-token math looks like when using prefix cache + batching.

[10:00] Samir: i'll paraphrase with an example. assume a 900-token prefix + 100-token generation. without cache you're paying compute for 1000 tokens per request. with KV prefetch you pay once to materialize the KV for the session (amortized over turns) then ~100 tokens per subsequent request. with batching you'll combine many suffix generations into a larger batch so concurrency vs latency tradeoffs apply.

[11:30] Diego: can we amortize prefetch across multiple users? e.g., same product context across many requests?

[12:00] Lena: prefix is per-session or per-key. you can design a shared session key — e.g., product_view:{product_id} — if the state is identical then it's shared. console has an example pattern under Optimize -> Cache keys. caution: correctness & personalization implications.

[13:45] Maya: show us the console please.

[14:10] Lena: sure, pulling up the Optimize tab — apologies if the WiFi hiccups. here i have your sample scenario prefilled: model: rw-large-3 (verified), seq dist: prefix 800–1200, generation 80–150. recommendations: enable prefix prefetch TTL 24h for product-level keys, prefetch cost threshold 2x expected turns, and batching target 16 tokens per batch for p90 latency.

[16:02] Samir: i want to highlight the Optimize 'cost projection' card — it shows estimated monthly token compute and the delta from enabling prefetch. in this template we see 46% token compute reduction for steady-state sessions after turn 1, and a 20–30% net invoice reduction when accounting for prefetch overhead at your traffic mix.

[17:15] Diego: that 46% number — what's the sensitivity? like if average session only has 2 turns, that amortization doesn't hold.

[17:50] Lena: exactly. Optimize has a knob to input average turns per session; in the sheet we ran three scenarios: 1. low-turn (1.7 turns) -> only 12% savings, 2. medium-turn (3.6) -> ~40% savings, 3. high-turn (8+) -> 60%+. i'll send the sim CSV.

[19:10] Priya: about batching — our p90 SLO is 200 ms, our infra adds ~40 ms network. can batching at the executor push p90 beyond budget?

[20:00] Lena: batching increases per-token throughput but can add queueing delay. Redwood supports latency targets: you set a max-queue-ms and batching will fill until either tokens/batch or max-queue is hit. default we recommend 12–20 ms max-queue for sub-200 ms budgets. Also continuous batching (micro-batches per GPU) helps keep tail low.

[21:40] Maya: any fallback if prefetch fails or cache is stale?
